selector:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create an original premium industrial-design storyboard for MagicDesk, strongly referencing Atomic Heart's Soviet retrofuturist laboratory machines: smooth milk-white glazed porcelain, polished nickel skeletons, dark steel, tiny oxide-red enamel details, expressive mechanical anatomy. The provided HELIOS image is the actual current product and the shared pedestal design reference. Preserve the low circular stepped pedestal and the HELIOS egg above it as context; this is a proposed physical modification to its pedestal, not a website UI.

Design a built-in MODEL ARCHIVE mechanism in the LEFT-FRONT SHOULDER of the base, separate from a RED X exit switch on the far right. A flush ivory push-lock with a stacked-plate symbol opens a curved shutter. A visible little telescoping metal rail extends diagonally left-front, carrying SIX visible miniature rigid smoked-glass archive plaques in thin nickel frames. They fan out like a precision mechanical Rolodex, each connected by a visible hinge to the rail, easy to distinguish and face the user. Each plaque displays an amber etched line silhouette of a different sculpture and ONLY one letter from A B C D E F. Plaques are physical glass/metal parts, NOT floating hologram UI rectangles; etched light can illuminate the glass. No left/right buttons or navigation arrows. When retracted the mechanism is flush and inconspicuous. Expanded plaques stay beside the machine, clear of the front controls, model, and red X.

Make a beautiful large 3:2 charcoal studio board with FOUR clearly divided views:
top left 'SEALED': tight three-quarter close-up of the base with a flush archive lock, egg partially visible above.
top right 'DEPLOY': the same base showing the curved shutter open and the linked plaque fan deployed, six clear plaque faces visible, egg retained.
bottom left 'SELECT': closer view of the same fan, G plaque tilted slightly toward user and glowing warmer, visible mechanical hinges and receiver slot; not a detached tablet.
bottom right 'CONTROL CASSETTE': cutaway close-up of a DIFFERENT functional feature in the center front fascia: a curved control cassette mechanically rotating inward on a drum. Expose its axle and track. Show old HELIOS round-button panel rotating below the rim while a dimensional-book panel with three ceramic page paddles, a toothed thumbwheel and red guarded seal-toggle rotates into view. Base body and red X stay fixed; the entire control arrangement changes, not just printed symbols.

Composition and lighting must prioritize readable machinery, large detail, attractive purposeful industrial geometry and spatial plausibility. No hands, people, text walls, logos, magic glyphs, blue-purple neon, levitating base, touchscreen menu, video game HUD, or concept render masquerading as real screenshot. Exact overall heading 'MAGICDESK  /  MECHANICAL ARCHIVE'.
The full library contains twelve devices, A through L. A mechanical archive carousel stores twelve plaques but exposes only six at once, with the remaining plaques visibly tucked in the rear of the drum. A ridged index spindle can be turned or scrolled to bring the other plaques forward. Do not add left/right buttons. In SELECT view select plaque E instead of G if needed for consistency; labels are small single letters, no menus.
transition:
Use case: stylized-concept. A cinematic industrial-design storyboard for MagicDesk illustrating a proposed model-change animation. Art style: Atomic Heart inspired Soviet retrofuture experimental laboratory, beautiful smooth milk-white porcelain, nickel anatomy, dark steel, oxide-red controls, restrained hot red/amber electromagnetic light, charcoal studio. Original designs, no copied game logos.

Reference 1 is the ACTUAL HELIOS egg and common pedestal. Reference 2 is the PALIMPSEST ENGINE concept with its unique page-paddle/roller control panel. Treat both as design references. Create six equally sized frames in a clean 3-column by 2-row board, with the exact same camera and common pedestal physical size, silhouette and floor position in every frame. Title 'MAGICDESK  /  ARCHIVE & RECAST'. Exact small frame titles '01 SELECT', '02 STOW', '03 ARCHIVE', '04 CASSETTE', '05 REBUILD', '06 ARRIVE'. No other text. Clear visual storytelling, cinematic but believable real-time effect vocabulary.

01 SELECT: HELIOS egg fully closed on base, a small real hinged fan of physical etched-glass model plaques has extended from the left-front base shoulder; chosen book plaque glows amber.
02 STOW: egg locks shut, red energy in cracks subsides, any residual steam dissipates naturally. Base and red X unchanged; no explosion.
03 ARCHIVE: three very small actual scanner heads have risen from rim sockets; a THIN horizontal red scan layer is midway down the egg. Above it the egg has converted to delicate vertical nickel-red filaments streaming down toward the mounting port; below it original solid porcelain/metal still clearly exists. Do not scale the egg into a little toy or hide it with smoke.
04 CASSETTE: same base with upper model almost fully archived, only a few fine scanning strands remain. In the front fascia the whole curved button cassette visibly turns inward on a real drum axle while the replacement cassette with ceramic page-paddles and an index thumbwheel turns forward. Permanent base outer shell and separate red X remain fixed.
05 REBUILD: book model reconstructs BOTTOM UP from its actual central spine: solid nickel/ivory folio below a thin ascending red scan plane, delicate incomplete wireframe upper cover edges above it. No simultaneous old egg. A few connected orange light contours emphasize registration, no giant magic portal or white flash.
06 ARRIVE: final coherent PALIMPSEST ENGINE folio on same base with book control panel fully locked into place, one cover slightly opens in a short greeting. Archive plaque fan folded back into its flush base hatch. Scanner heads retract.

Keep the common base completely stable across shots, tiny scanned particles stay in a compact volume, coherent actuator connections. No cursor, no app window border, no floating UI, no leftright navigation controls, no blue-purple holographic screen, no explosions, no arbitrary morph between egg and book. This is a concept storyboard, not actual program evidence.
transition_revision:
Edit this six-frame transition storyboard for MECHANICAL CONSISTENCY. Preserve the six-frame layout, same pedestal exterior dimensions, same camera, red scanning effect and egg-to-book transition.
1. In frames 01 SELECT, 02 STOW and 03 ARCHIVE, the base front panel must be the ORIGINAL HELIOS panel: seven round tactile buttons, far-right red X. Currently it incorrectly already shows book paddles. Change it back to round buttons in these first THREE frames only.
2. In frame 04 CASSETTE show the old ROUND-BUTTON panel rotating inward on left and the new THREE IVORY PAGE-PADDLES + index wheel + guarded red seal panel rotating outward at center. They are different physical panels, not two copies of the book panel.
3. The tall ceramic valve/pillar sticking up at the far right belongs to the OLD EGG, not to the shared base. It must dematerialize with the egg in frame 03 and must be ABSENT in frames 04,05,06. Similarly old egg-specific hydraulic struts must be gone in 04-06; only the common circular pedestal and the new book's OWN short central mount remain.
4. Frames 05 and 06 retain the new book control cassette. The physical shared pedestal shell and red X stay stable across every frame.
5. In frame 01 the selected small archive plaque should depict a BOOK silhouette, not an egg.
No redesign of the main egg or book. Same Atomic Heart inspired milk-white porcelain, nickel and red industrial aesthetic. Keep headings and typography unchanged. This is a storyboard, not a screenshot.
status: Conceptual: no internal packaging or mechanical fit has yet been verified.
